title: U.S. House · Wisconsin's 4th Congressional District
area: The city of Milwaukee and near suburbs.

context.text: Incumbent Gwen Moore (D) defeated Amy Donahue 70.5%-29.3% in the Democratic primary. Tim Rogers advanced from the Republican primary. Arthur Burks also qualified as an independent for the general-election ballot; two other independents, Carlos Dixon and Robert Raymond, withdrew or were disqualified.

candidates.name: Gwen Moore
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated Amy Donahue 70.5%-29.3% in the Democratic primary.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Wisconsin's 4th Congressional District (since 2005)

summary.text: Gwen Moore is the Democratic incumbent representing Wisconsin's 4th District (Milwaukee) since 2005, the first African American elected to Congress from Wisconsin. Before Congress she was a VISTA volunteer, a housing and social services official, and a state legislator for 15 years. She serves on the House Ways and Means Committee and the Joint Economic Committee and is seeking another term.

background.text: Born in Racine, Wisconsin, in 1951 and raised in Milwaukee, the eighth of nine children; her father was a union factory worker and her mother a public school teacher. She attended North Division High School in Milwaukee, where she was student council president.

Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Marquette University, which she says she attended as a single, expectant mother with help from the federal TRIO program; she later earned a Harvard University Certificate for Senior Executives in State and Local Government in 2000. Sources differ on the year of her Marquette degree.
As a VISTA volunteer, helped start a community credit union and received the national "VISTA Volunteer of the Decade" award for 1976-1986, according to her official biography.

Worked as a housing officer for the Wisconsin Housing Development Authority; WUWM, drawing on her campaign website, says she worked for the City of Milwaukee and the state on housing and social services issues.
Served two terms in the Wisconsin State Assembly (1989-1992) and in the Wisconsin State Senate from 1993 to 2004.

Elected to the U.S. House in 2004, defeating Republican attorney Gerald Boyle with 69.6% of the vote according to Wikipedia, and became the first African American elected to Congress from Wisconsin; she took office on January 3, 2005.

Serves on the House Ways and Means Committee (Tax, Social Security, and Work and Welfare subcommittees) and the Joint Economic Committee, and co-chairs the bipartisan Congressional Caucus on Foster Youth. She previously served on the Financial Services, Science, Space, and Technology, and Budget committees.
Served as Democratic co-chair of the Congressional Women's Caucus from 2011 to 2013 and is a member of the Congressional Black Caucus and the Congressional Progressive Caucus, among others.
Won the August 11, 2026 Democratic primary over Amy Donahue, 70.5% to 29.3%. WUWM describes her as Wisconsin's longest-serving current member of the state's U.S. House delegation.
According to her official biography, she is the mother of three and a grandmother and great-grandmother.

record.text: Serves on the Joint Economic Committee and the House Committee on Ways and Means (Social Security, Tax, and Work and Welfare subcommittees) in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.researchNotes: Her official website lists issue areas (economy and jobs, health care, immigration, environment, veterans, among others) but no extractable position statements were found as of the research date.

candidates.name: Tim Rogers

summary.text: Tim Rogers is the Republican nominee for Wisconsin's 4th District. A Milwaukee native who works delivering gift baskets and newspapers for two local businesses, he has run for this seat in every election since 2018. His campaign website lists universal school choice, criminal justice reform, clean water and lower taxes as priorities.

background.text: Born and lives in Milwaukee, Wisconsin; graduated from North Division High School in 1978 and studied at the University of Wisconsin-Parkside and Milwaukee Area Technical College.
Works delivering gift baskets and newspapers for two local businesses, according to WUWM, which drew on his campaign website and earlier news coverage.

Ran as the Republican nominee against Gwen Moore in 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2024, losing each general election. In 2024 he won the Republican primary over Purnima Nath, 71.2% to 28.4%, and received 22.4% in the general election.
Said in 2024 that he made a commitment in 2018 to keep running "until we get it right."
Won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary over Purnima Nath.

candidates.researchNotes: Rogers has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and no current campaign website statements on issues were found as of the research date.

candidates.name: Arthur Burks

summary.text: Arthur Burks is an independent candidate for Wisconsin's 4th District. According to his campaign website, as described by WUWM, he has been rooted in Milwaukee since the 1970s and has run several businesses there. He is running on living wages, local business investment, gun safety legislation and housing access.

background.text: According to his campaign website, as reported by WUWM, he has been rooted in Milwaukee since the 1970s, has run many successful businesses there, and raised a family in the city.
His campaign website says he has been active in the National Action Network; WUWM reports the organization would not confirm his membership or participation.
Did not answer WUWM's candidate questionnaire and has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey; qualified for the November 2026 ballot as an independent.
